samples.sample_label: 0.02Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot prepared by induction melting in a water-cooled copper crucible; re-melted and swiftly poured into a rotating copper mold at high speed to obtain steel strips with dimensions 60 × 70 × 2.5 mm through near-rapid solidification.
Extended aging treatment at 723 K for 6 h on the as-cast steel strip; part of the study of aging period effect at 723 K.

structures.overall_structure: Ferrite (δ) dispersed in austenite (γ) matrix; phase boundaries between ferrite and austenite become irregular with numerous irregular bulges after prolonged 723 K aging.

phases_present.morphology: irregularly shaped ferrite dispersed in austenite matrix

precipitates.distribution: submicron white particles within the austenite matrix

interfaces.phase_evolution: As the aging time prolongs, the phase boundaries between ferrite and austenite become irregular, featuring numerous irregular bulges; no significant change in the volume fraction of constituent phases.
interfaces.interface_notes: Prolonged 723 K aging roughens the ferrite/austenite interfaces; ferrite content in 0.02Nb steel aged 723 K/6 h is 17.1 vol%.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge width 4 mm; gauge length 12 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: a minimum of four repetitions per steel strip

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength and total elongation at 723 K/6 h

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases in the 0.02Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: Primary phases remain ferrite and austenite; no observable new diffraction peak after 723 K/6 h aging.

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with EBSD detector
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EBSD scanning step size 300 nm; samples electropolished with 10 vol% perchloric acid alcohol solution at 25 V for 10 s
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe microstructure of the 0.02Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregular ferrite dispersed in austenite matrix; phase boundaries irregular with bulges; submicron NbC particles present; ferrite content 17.1 vol%.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ambient temperature; strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1; gauge width 4 mm; gauge length 12 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure tensile properties of the 0.02Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: Yield strength 950 ± 14 MPa, tensile strength 1081 ± 18 MPa, total elongation 28 ± 1 %.

computational_details.simulation_method: Spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) within generalized gradient approximation (GGA) using first-principles Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE) recipe
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Projector augmented wave (PAW) potentials; plane-wave basis set with kinetic energy cutoff 500 eV; Gaussian smearing width 0.05 eV; U = 2.59 eV for Fe atoms
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 2 × 2 × 2 atomic supercell of κ-carbide (Fe3AlC, E21 structure); vacuum spacing 15 Å; 6 × 6 × 6 Monkhorst–Pack k-point sampling; convergence criterion energy change below 0.03 eV Å^-1

analytical_models.model_note: Nb doping of κ-carbide significantly increases its formation energy; the values are alloy-level DFT results used to explain reduced κ-carbide formation in Nb-containing steels.

analytical_models.model_name: Diffusion coefficients of Al and C in austenite
analytical_models.equation_role: Calculated diffusion coefficients of Al and C in austenite for 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels over 673–873 K
analytical_models.model_note: Nb atoms slightly decrease the diffusion coefficient of C in austenite (strong Nb–C affinity) and slightly increase the Al diffusion coefficient; slower C diffusion decelerates κ-carbide nucleation and growth.

unmapped_findings: The paper does not report κ-carbide size/volume fraction specifically for the 0.02Nb steel aged at 723 K/6 h; quantitative κ-carbide values for 723 K/6 h and 9 h are given only for the 0.04Nb steel (18.7 and 19.5 vol%; 7 and 9 nm) [b0044].

Austenite grain size of the as-cast 0.02Nb steel is 18 μm and ferrite grain size is 3.6 μm; the paper states the austenite grain size remains almost unchanged after aging at 823 K/3 h, but no grain size is reported specifically for the 723 K/6 h state [b0031].
Measured strip composition of the 0.02Nb steel (Table 1): Mn 12.80, Al 9.01, Cr 3.01, C 1.39, Nb 0.021, Fe balance (wt%) [b0014, b0015].
Austenite matrix composition of the as-cast 0.02Nb steel (Table 4): Mn 13.12, Al 8.35, Cr 4.06, C 1.39, Nb 0.019, Fe 63.79 wt% [b0067, b0073, b0074].
Microhardness values are reported only for as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h and 823 K/3 h states (0.02Nb: 406, 440, 455, 467 HV); no microhardness is reported for the 723 K/6 h state [b0034].
The engineering stress–strain curve of the 0.02Nb steel aged at 723 K/6 h (Figure 13, red curve) yields just above 900 MPa and plateaus close to 1200 MPa, extending to about 28% strain [figure_013].
